clue.text: Plain-spoken, but not sharp

definitions.meaning: a frank, direct speaker who does not soften what they say
a dull edge or point, like an old knife

explanation.surface: Someone is described as outspoken though perhaps not very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one adjective: candid in speech, and having a dulled edge.

clue.text: Spanish uncle in south-western county displays piety

indicators.note: the uncle is placed inside the county's name, as the clue's 'in' says

parts.note: Devon is a county in the south-west of England
tio is Spanish for uncle

explanation.surface: A Spanish relative living in the West Country shows religious devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; 'uncle' looks like a family member in the surface but needs translating into Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious devotion and piety are both reverent, dutiful worship.

clue.text: About to depart after partition

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to leave is to depart

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to go once a country has been divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to depart' reads as one idea, someone on the point of leaving, but 'About' is just C (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split apart, which is what a partition does to something.

clue.text: Security for Fleming's hero

definitions.meaning: a ... is a pledge or guarantee given as security, such as a bail ...

explanation.surface: A request for protection for the famous fictional spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee lodged as surety, and the secret agent created by novelist Ian Fleming.

clue.text: Battered woman in German spa

indicators.note: the woman is placed inside the spa town's name, as 'in' says

parts.note: Bad is the German word for bath, used in spa town names like Baden-Baden
she is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A bruised woman is found at a German health resort.
explanation.walkthrough: German spa towns carry the prefix Bad (bath), as in Bad Ems; 'Battered woman' wants to be read together but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered and bashed both mean struck hard and repeatedly.

clue.text: West African gourmand subject to experiments

parts.note: Guinea is a country in West Africa
a pig is a greedy eater, a glutton

explanation.surface: A greedy eater from West Africa is used in scientific tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing used as the trial case in testing is idiomatically called this, after the lab rodent.

clue.text: Despondent dandy with illustrious parentage

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling low
a blood is an old word for a fashionable young man about town

explanation.surface: A gloomy fop who comes from a distinguished family.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOOD is an old-fashioned word for a dandy or rake.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocratic descent is traditionally called this, from the noble's supposedly bluish veins.

clue.text: Left a young animal to drink

parts.note: a pup is a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a puppy to have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to drink eagerly with the tongue, as a cat does milk.

clue.text: Panic about the copperhead is rare

indicators.note: the panic word goes around the copper's head letter, as 'about' says

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
the head (first letter) of copper is C

explanation.surface: Alarm over a venomous snake, which is seldom seen.
explanation.walkthrough: A copperhead is a snake, but here it means the head of 'copper', its first letter C, which goes inside SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, so seldom found.

clue.text: An attempt by painter to get fine wool

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter in crosswords

explanation.surface: A painter tries to obtain good-quality yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft yarn spun from the hair of a particular goat or rabbit breed.

clue.text: Marine jobber has two lots of cards

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of playing cards
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A sailor-for-hire carries a couple of packs of playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The two lots are a DECK (the whole pack) and a HAND (one player's share).
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman who does manual work aboard ship is a marine labourer.

clue.text: Mum is retiring before pre-Easter period

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Mother is going to bed before Lent begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns IS into SI; 'Mum' is not a mother here but the word for keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means saying nothing, being quiet.

clue.text: Hardly the undergarment for president Roosevelt!

definitions.meaning: a woman's one-piece undergarment combining camisole and knickers
Theodore Roosevelt, US president, was nicknamed this

explanation.surface: A joke that a lacy one-piece would hardly suit Theodore Roosevelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A lingerie item and the nickname of the US president who also gave his name to the toy bear.

clue.text: MP reveals labour farming policy

parts.note: red is the colour of the Labour party, standing for the left
CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy

explanation.surface: A politician unveils his party's agriculture plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like a Member of Parliament, but it is a military policeman, nicknamed a REDCAP in Britain for the red hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A British military policeman is nicknamed for the red cover on his cap.

clue.text: Domestic alarm system used by old defence force

parts.note: home means domestic, as in home affairs
a guard is a protective device or watchman

explanation.surface: A burglar alarm installed by a former military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The HOME GUARD was Britain's volunteer local defence force in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The volunteer militia that protected Britain against invasion in World War Two.

clue.text: Proceed from Tobago onward to Trinidad

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words Tobago onward, running across them

explanation.surface: Travel on from one Caribbean island to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'Tobago' and the start of 'onward'; 'to Trinidad' only completes the travel picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on or continue is to proceed.

clue.text: Mark is told to invest German capital

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning told or ordered

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word German is taken

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark is instructed to put money into Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' suggests Berlin, but it is the capital letter G; 'invest' means surround, so BADE (told) goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or sign, a distinguishing mark.

clue.text: Coach and family are given the boot

parts.note: a coach is a bus for long trips
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A coach company and its relations are dismissed from their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the boot' suggests being sacked, but the boot is the footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A buskin is a calf-high laced boot, worn by actors in classical tragedy.

clue.text: Understand it's time to get a hairpiece

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, as in physics
a wig is a hairpiece

explanation.surface: A balding man realises it is time to buy a toupee.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British slang for grasping or catching on.

clue.text: A list prepared by fellow displaying charm

indicators.note: prepared means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man has drawn up a list and shows his appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' makes TALIS, the anagram of A LIST; 'charm' suggests charisma but is a lucky object.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky amulet or object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Unusually scared of trees

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is strangely frightened of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Large evergreen conifers, such as those of Lebanon.

clue.text: A poorly-made article in Iran

definitions.note: the definition names a place located in Iran

parts.note: something badly made is bad
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shoddy item is found in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a location, a place in Iran: ABADAN is an oil-refining city on the Persian Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: A port and oil-refining city in south-west Iran on the Shatt al-Arab.

clue.text: Youth leader meets prior every twelvemonth

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of youth

parts.note: prior means earlier, so early is a fair synonym

explanation.surface: A young leader meets a monastery prior once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' looks like a monk, but it means earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Annually, occurring once every year.

clue.text: A physician went ahead — but slowly

definitions.text: A physician went ahead — but slowly

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A doctor walks in front at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: MB is the Bachelor of Medicine degree; LED (went ahead) completes it, and the whole clue describes strolling.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at an easy, leisurely pace.

clue.text: Money always gives one purchasing power

definitions.note: purchase is mechanical advantage or grip, so this is a tool giving it

parts.note: L stands for pound (libra), money
ever means always

explanation.surface: Cash at all times lets you buy things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchasing power' suggests spending money, but purchase here means mechanical grip or leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar pivoted on a fulcrum gives mechanical advantage, a firm grip to shift heavy loads.

clue.text: Medicine taken by churchman around teatime

indicators.note: the churchman is placed around the teatime letters, as 'around' says

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman
teatime is four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A vicar takes his tonic at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime is traditionally four o'clock, so it gives the Roman numeral for four; 'Medicine' is used as a noun for a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A curative is a remedy, something that heals.

clue.text: Students sit it in the afternoon

definitions.meaning: read as ex-a.m., no longer morning, so after noon

explanation.surface: Pupils take their test after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: EX (former) + AM (morning) means a time no longer in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A test students take, and a punning reading as formerly morning, so afternoon.

clue.text: Outwitted the finest newspaper's chief

parts.note: best means finest
Ed is short for editor, a newspaper's chief

explanation.surface: A top newspaper's editor was outsmarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bested means got the better of, beaten.

clue.text: Imagine having 500+500 pages!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Picture a huge book a thousand pages long.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 500 is D in Roman numerals; the second, with pages, is a REAM of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to fancy or picture in the mind.

clue.text: Flimsy fabric reckoned to have been ripped

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
rated means reckoned, valued

explanation.surface: A delicate fabric is judged to be torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means torn or ripped open, of flesh.
